open_questions: Centroid remains inconclusive with no clear difference image and centroid_all not_run - follow-up high-resolution imaging would confirm on-target location.

Phase curve amplitude 2409 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.2293 with star rotation amplitudes 14025 ppm and 17036 ppm - stellar activity of this M dwarf needs to be monitored but does not match variability period as rotation 0.966 d vs signal 13.3757 d.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows 3 consistent 0.09% flat-bottomed dips every 13.4 days around an M-dwarf 81 ly away, implying a 3.8 Earth-radius mini-Neptune. No odd-even difference, no secondary eclipse, and depths repeat steadily across sectors with no nearby star able to mimic the signal. Variability from the star's own 0.97-day rotation is present but at a different period than the dips.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) favours planet transit over V-shaped grazing binary.
Planet-sized at 3.846 Rearth, consistent with mini-Neptune, not stellar.
No odd/even difference; no secondary (snr 3.545 below 5) and phase-curve at 13.4 d not significant.
Three transits depths consistent and sectors p_constant 0.20195272772844286 steady; depth does not change between sectors.
No neighbour within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly cause dip, closest needs 29.2 arcsec sep, point to on-target.
Duration 2.998 h vs central 2.143 h ratio 1.399 fits for 13.4 d orbit (b=0.2326), for M-dwarf star Teff 3007 K Rad 0.3418.
